steps.text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add white potatoes and sweet potato; cook in boiling water until a knife is easily inserted into the centers, about 30 minutes. Drain, cool, peel, and chop potatoes into bite-sized pieces.

Place eggs in a saucepan and cover with cold water. Bring water to a boil. Cover, remove from heat, and let eggs stand in hot water until fully hard cooked, 10 to 12 minutes. Remove from hot water; cool, peel, and chop into bite-sized pieces.
Combine potatoes, eggs, celery, and onion in a large serving bowl.
Whisk together mayonnaise, mustard, pepper, and salt in a small bowl until well combined. Add to potato mixture and stir to coat. Refrigerate and serve chilled.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Potato Potato Salad
raw_recipe.description: This sweet potato salad is made with white potatoes and sweet potatoes, mayonnaise, a bit of mustard, celery, and hard-boiled eggs for a unique, tasty salad.

review.reviewBody: This came out really, really well . Very pretty, and everyone commented. However, with all these cold, mayonnaise-based salads, I always cut the mayo in half and use a light sour cream for the other. To me, it makes it creamier and a lot healthier without sacraficing taste. Everyone appreciates it, too. With the added mustard, it is really perfect. I salt (everything) very lightly and sprinkled a really good layer of pepper over the potatoes. Also, I used only half the eggs. The celery adds a welcome crunch. Make a big batch so you can enjoy it for a few days! Thanks Dee.

Since potato salad isn't one of my top 10 favorites, I was looking for a change to the standard. This is a good recipe and I agree with others who mentioned that it could use more flavor. I used only sweet potatoes. I peeled and cubed them before cooking so cooking time was only about 10 minutes (even with a larger cut I think 30 minutes would give you mush), plus I cooked them in chicken broth instead of water. Immediately after draining I spread them on a cookie sheet, and drizzled with a mixture of 2 Tbsp mustard and 2 Tbsp cider vinegar. I tossed the potatoes in this (The hot potatoes soak up a great deal of flavor this way) and then refrigerated them for about 30 minutes. Then I added them to the celery, egg and onion (I used a medium sized Vidalia and used the whole thing). I used half mayo and half sour cream and cut the mayo mixture with some milk to make it thinner. Even with the flavorful potatoes and the whole onion, it is still pretty bland. Next time I think I'll go with a stronger onion and maybe consider a Dijon mustard or one with horseradish. It's a good start but not quite a 5 star for us.

didnt have celery so substituted fresh steamed green beans. used one large sweet potato, one smaller russet, and 3 chopped eggs. I'm on an acid free diet, so used mustard powder and tons of dill weed, garlic powder and celery seed to make up for the loss of the prepared mustard which has vinegar. Thanks for the recipe
I made this but I roasted the potatoes in the oven for about 25 minutes instead of boiling them. It is a really good recipe!

Love the taste, colours and crunch of the celery. I used red onion, which gave extra colour, a third of the the mayo (topping it up with natural Greek yogurt), cut back to a teaspoon of whole grain mustard, a pinch of salt and a small amount of ground black pepper, as a life style choice. Surrounded the bowl with sliced tomatoes and cucumber. DELISH!

One of the best potato salad recipes ever! So easy to make and healthier then the store bought salad. I did reduce the amount of mayonnaise by 1/4 cup and used a sweet onion which didn't give it that onion taste. Also, I pulled the sweet potatoes out about 5-10 mins early because they cooked much faster then the regular brown potatoes. All in all, a wonderful recipe!

Excellent salad recipe! Definitely will make again. Took to a family gathering and everyone wanted the recipe. Disclaimer: I made quite a few additions... due to dietary restrictions... added chopped orange peppers, sugar snap peas, pickles and bacon. It had enough of the flavors of my mom's traditional potatoe salad to make it feel reminiscent and indulgant without the extra carbs and calories! My family loved the extra crunch of the snap peas! Can't wait to make this again!
Easy to make and tastes good. I used spring onions for a fresher effect and added frozen peas for more colour.

If you are a beginner like me, and over boiled your potatoes and they are all mushy. Once you've cubed them, throw them on a cookie sheet and throw them in the freezer until they are somewhat stiff. That way it doesn't mush even more when you mix it all in with the mayo mix. Thanks for the recipe :)

This is a WINNER! I tweaked a bit by adding a teaspoon of curry to the mayo mix & about a tablespoon of sugar...I also seasoned the potatoes with garlic powder, onion powder, cracked black pepper, seasoning salt (teaspoon each). Perfect! Was a crowd pleaser at my pre-Thanksgiving party. Several requests for the recipe.

I liked this a lot. I do think it's a bit too peppery. I reduced it to about a tsp. and think it'd be better with even less. It got rave reviews by our dinner guests as well! We did use 2 sweet potatoes and 1 red potato. I also used 1/3 T yellow mustard, 1/3 T coarse ground mustard and 1/3 T spicy brown mustard. Thanks for the recipe!
Great flavor. Almost like a curried potato salad!
I had this at a tea room one time and this is so unique. Really like it.
I have made it several times with guests and it’s always a great hit
Don’t think I will ever eat potato salad the same way again…..this is Amazing

Looked this up after having something similar at a friends house. Her recipe added sweet relish (to emphasize the sweet potato). I didnt have sweet so I added a couple TBSP of dill relish, and it turned out great! Another reviewer was wondering "what was missing" so I'd suggest adding a spoon or 2 of pickle relish, sweet or dill, your choice!
This doesn't seem to be something I really want to make again

I found the recipe to be quite good! With the tweaks recommended from another commenter, it definitely improved the flavor. I couldn't help feeling that it's still missing a kick. Still--I love that this is an easy recipe to follow and uses sweet potatoes without making them sweet or into desserts!
Not bad.
The absolute best 👌
